doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: What Les Paul invented
summary: Pallo describes Les Paul's trapeze tailpiece, solid body, work with Gibson and ongoing experimenting at 91.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Right. Well after all, I was never quite sure, what exactly did he — he invented the Les Paul guitar? What exactly was it that he did for the guitar? Do you recall?

Let’s see. I know he does have a patent on the trapeze tailpiece, that’s the bottom of the guitar. That he has a patent on. He did some innovation on, well the Les Paul guitar, more of a solid body, because he had what we call the railroad track, as he calls it, he put a string on the railroad track and the vibration of it and the sound of it sustains and so forth. That’s where you come in with the solid body. And then with Gibson he worked with Ted McCarty and together they made the Les Paul guitar, and that was I think, I’m not too sure of the year. In the fifties is when the first one came out.
Yeah. A pretty innovative guy, he did the stuff with the tape overdubbing.

Oh that’s another part yeah, that’s the electronic part. And Les is still experimenting today. He still doesn’t stop at 91 years old. He is always trying, puts the pick-up on top of the guitar, on the bottom and sideways, on angles, and tried everything. It’s always, like we were just talking about music itself, you never stop learning. He’ll never stop learning. And it’s great too. It’s great to keep learning. You just taught me something too, today, you told me about the piano.
